title: Rich vs Poor Countries Adventure
welcome_lead: Why are some countries rich and others poor? 🌏
meta_desc: Global Economy Adventure 3 — KS3 Economics on development and global inequality.
final_note: You learned about rich and poor countries, GDP and what helps countries develop.

walkthroughs.body_html:
GDP measures everything a country makes.

USA, China and Germany have huge GDP. Small countries can have small GDP but still be rich per person.

Developed countries (UK, Japan) have good schools, hospitals and infrastructure.

Developing countries are still growing — they may have weaker services and lower wages.

The gap is called inequality.

Rich countries often give aid:

  • Cash for emergencies.
  • Loans for schools and roads.
  • Doctors and engineers.

The goal: sustainable growth that doesn't wreck the planet. 🌱

mcqs.q: What is the difference between nominal and real values?
options: Nominal means estimated and real means accurate.
QE is when banks charge negative interest on deposits.
Nominal values are measured in current money; real values are adjusted for inflation to allow meaningful comparison over time.
Nominal values are written and real values are spent.

mcqs.q: How does quantitative easing actually work?
options: QE is when banks charge negative interest on deposits.

The central bank creates reserves to buy financial assets (mostly government bonds) from banks and pension funds, raising asset prices and lowering yields — stimulating spending and lending indirectly. It is not literally printing physical cash for the public.
Opportunity cost is the money price of something.
QE is the central bank printing money and handing it to citizens.
Opportunity cost is the total of everything you give up when making a choice.
Nominal values are written and real values are spent.
The value of the next-best alternative foregone when a choice is made — the real cost of a decision in terms of what you give up.
Opportunity cost is the money price of something.
